-- db/schema.sql
-- Repository Intelligence Layer — Complete PostgreSQL Schema
-- Idempotent: safe to run multiple times (CREATE IF NOT EXISTS throughout)

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- EXTENSIONS  (must come first)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pgcrypto";
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pg_trgm";

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LAYER 0: REPOSITORIES
-- One row per scanned root directory.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS repositories (
    id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    name        TEXT        NOT NULL,
    root_path   TEXT        NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    language    TEXT,
    indexed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LAYER 1A: FILES
-- One row per source file. file_hash drives incremental indexing.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS files (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    repository_id   INT         NOT NULL REFERENCES repositories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    path            TEXT        NOT NULL,
    relative_path   TEXT        NOT NULL,
    language        TEXT,
    file_hash       TEXT        NOT NULL,       -- sha256; changes trigger re-index
    size_bytes      BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    modified_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    indexed_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    symbols_indexed BOOL        DEFAULT FALSE,  -- true after symbol extraction
    embedded        BOOL        DEFAULT FALSE,  -- true after embedding
    UNIQUE (repository_id, relative_path)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_files_repo         ON files(repository_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_files_language     ON files(language);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_files_hash         ON files(file_hash);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_files_dirty        ON files(symbols_indexed, embedded);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LAYER 1B: SYMBOLS
-- AST-extracted symbols: CLASS / METHOD / FUNCTION / INTERFACE / ENUM
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS symbols (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    file_id         INT         NOT NULL REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    repository_id   INT         NOT NULL REFERENCES repositories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name            TEXT        NOT NULL,
    qualified_name  TEXT,
    symbol_type     TEXT        NOT NULL,       -- CLASS | METHOD | FUNCTION | INTERFACE | ENUM
    parent_name     TEXT,
    line_start      INT,
    line_end        INT,
    signature       TEXT,
    language        TEXT        NOT NULL,
    indexed_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_symbols_name         ON symbols(name);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_symbols_type         ON symbols(symbol_type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_symbols_file         ON symbols(file_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_symbols_repo         ON symbols(repository_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_symbols_parent       ON symbols(parent_name);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_symbols_qualified    ON symbols(qualified_name);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_symbols_name_trgm
    ON symbols USING gin(name gin_trgm_ops);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LAYER 2: SYMBOL RELATIONSHIPS
-- Directed edges between symbols (or files when symbol is unknown).
--
-- rel_type values:
--   EXTENDS      — class A extends class B
--   IMPLEMENTS   — class A implements interface B
--   CALLS        — method A calls method B
--   USES         — file/symbol A imports/uses file/symbol B
--   TESTS        — test class/method A tests production class/method B
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS symbol_relationships (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    repository_id   INT         NOT NULL REFERENCES repositories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    -- source (the thing doing the extending / calling / testing)
    from_symbol_id  INT         REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    from_file_id    INT         REFERENCES files(id)   ON DELETE CASCADE,
    from_name       TEXT        NOT NULL,       -- human-readable, always set

    -- target (the thing being extended / called / tested)
    to_symbol_id    INT         REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    to_file_id      INT         REFERENCES files(id)   ON DELETE SET NULL,
    to_name         TEXT        NOT NULL,

    rel_type        TEXT        NOT NULL,       -- EXTENDS | IMPLEMENTS | CALLS | USES | TESTS
    confidence      REAL        DEFAULT 1.0,    -- 1.0 = AST-certain, <1.0 = heuristic
    indexed_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_repo         ON symbol_relationships(repository_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_from_sym     ON symbol_relationships(from_symbol_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_to_sym       ON symbol_relationships(to_symbol_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_from_file    ON symbol_relationships(from_file_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_type         ON symbol_relationships(rel_type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_from_name    ON symbol_relationships(from_name);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_to_name      ON symbol_relationships(to_name);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LAYER 3: EMBEDDINGS
-- One row per embedded symbol. Stores the vector as a float array.
-- Dimension: 384 (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
--
-- When pgvector is available, swap REAL[] for vector(384).
-- The application layer handles both cases.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS embeddings (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    symbol_id       INT         NOT NULL REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    repository_id   INT         NOT NULL REFERENCES repositories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    model           TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2',
    vector          REAL[]      NOT NULL,        -- 384-dim float array
    input_text      TEXT,                        -- the text that was embedded
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (symbol_id, model)                    -- one embedding per symbol per model
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_emb_symbol   ON embeddings(symbol_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_emb_repo     ON embeddings(repository_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_emb_model    ON embeddings(model);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LAYER 4: INDEX JOBS
-- Audit log for every indexing run.
-- Enables: "what changed since last run?", replay, debugging.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS index_jobs (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    repository_id   INT         NOT NULL REFERENCES repositories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    job_type        TEXT        NOT NULL,        -- FULL | INCREMENTAL | SYMBOLS | EMBEDDINGS
    status          TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',  -- running | done | failed
    files_scanned   INT         DEFAULT 0,
    files_changed   INT         DEFAULT 0,
    files_skipped   INT         DEFAULT 0,
    symbols_added   INT         DEFAULT 0,
    symbols_deleted INT         DEFAULT 0,
    embeddings_added INT        DEFAULT 0,
    relationships_added INT     DEFAULT 0,
    error_message   TEXT,
    started_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    finished_at     TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_jobs_repo    ON index_jobs(repository_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_jobs_status  ON index_jobs(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_jobs_type    ON index_jobs(job_type);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LAYER 5: TESTS
-- Links test files/symbols to the production code they test.
-- Populated by the relationship indexer (heuristic + naming conventions).
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tests (
    id                  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    repository_id       INT     NOT NULL REFERENCES repositories(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    -- the test
    test_file_id        INT     REFERENCES files(id)   ON DELETE CASCADE,
    test_symbol_id      INT     REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    test_name           TEXT    NOT NULL,

    -- what is being tested
    target_file_id      INT     REFERENCES files(id)   ON DELETE SET NULL,
    target_symbol_id    INT     REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    target_name         TEXT,

    detection_method    TEXT    DEFAULT 'naming_convention',  -- or 'annotation' or 'import'
    indexed_at          TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tests_repo           ON tests(repository_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tests_test_file      ON tests(test_file_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tests_target_file    ON tests(target_file_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tests_target_symbol  ON tests(target_symbol_id);

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- LAYER 6: REPAIR PATTERNS
-- Stores successful LLM repair actions as training signal.
-- When a similar failure recurs, the agent retrieves past repairs
-- and includes them in the prompt as few-shot examples.
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS repair_patterns (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    repository_id   INT         REFERENCES repositories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,

    -- failure fingerprint
    error_type      TEXT        NOT NULL,    -- NullPointerException | CompileError | TestFailure
    error_message   TEXT,                   -- short excerpt of the error
    failure_hash    TEXT,                   -- sha256(error_type + error_message) for dedup

    -- affected code
    file_path       TEXT,
    symbol_name     TEXT,
    broken_code     TEXT,                   -- the code BEFORE repair

    -- successful repair
    repaired_code   TEXT,                   -- the code AFTER repair
    patch_diff      TEXT,                   -- unified diff of the repair
    llm_model       TEXT,                   -- which LLM produced this repair

    -- outcome
    tests_passed    BOOL        DEFAULT FALSE,
    used_count      INT         DEFAULT 1,  -- how many times this pattern was reused
    last_used_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_repair_error_type    ON repair_patterns(error_type);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_repair_hash          ON repair_patterns(failure_hash);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_repair_symbol        ON repair_patterns(symbol_name);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_repair_repo          ON repair_patterns(repository_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_repair_passed        ON repair_patterns(tests_passed);

# editing/ast_locator.py
#
# Locates a symbol's exact AST node, start/end lines, and byte offsets.

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from tree_sitter import Language, Parser
import tree_sitter_java as ts_java
import tree_sitter_python as ts_python
import tree_sitter_javascript as ts_js
import tree_sitter_typescript as ts_typescript

@dataclass
class ASTNodeInfo:
    node_type: str
    name: str
    start_line: int  # 1-indexed
    end_line: int    # 1-indexed
    start_byte: int
    end_byte: int
    content: str

class ASTLocator:
    def __init__(self):
        # Initialize languages
        self.langs = {
            "java": Language(ts_java.language()),
            "python": Language(ts_python.language()),
            "javascript": Language(ts_js.language()),
            "typescript": Language(ts_typescript.language_typescript()),
            "tsx": Language(ts_typescript.language_tsx())
        }
        
    def get_language(self, file_path: str) -> str:
        ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)[1].lower()
        if ext == ".java":
            return "java"
        elif ext == ".py":
            return "python"
        elif ext == ".js" or ext == ".jsx":
            return "javascript"
        elif ext == ".ts":
            return "typescript"
        elif ext == ".tsx":
            return "tsx"
        return "unknown"

    def find_symbol(self, file_path: str, symbol_name: str, source: str = None) -> ASTNodeInfo | None:
        if source is None:
            with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                source = f.read()
                
        lang_str = self.get_language(file_path)
        lang = self.langs.get(lang_str)
        if not lang:
            # Fallback text block matcher if language not supported
            return self._fallback_match(source, symbol_name)

        parser = Parser(lang)
        src_bytes = source.encode("utf-8")
        tree = parser.parse(src_bytes)
        
        # Search the tree for nodes matching the symbol_name
        target_parts = symbol_name.split(".")
        
        found_node = self._find_matching_node(tree.root_node, target_parts, src_bytes)
        if found_node:
            start_line = found_node.start_point[0] + 1
            end_line = found_node.end_point[0] + 1
            content = src_bytes[found_node.start_byte:found_node.end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            return ASTNodeInfo(
                node_type=found_node.type,
                name=symbol_name,
                start_line=start_line,
                end_line=end_line,
                start_byte=found_node.start_byte,
                end_byte=found_node.end_byte,
                content=content
            )
        
        # Fallback suffix/substring matching if hierarchical matching failed
        found_node = self._find_any_matching_node(tree.root_node, target_parts[-1], src_bytes)
        if found_node:
            start_line = found_node.start_point[0] + 1
            end_line = found_node.end_point[0] + 1
            content = src_bytes[found_node.start_byte:found_node.end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            return ASTNodeInfo(
                node_type=found_node.type,
                name=symbol_name,
                start_line=start_line,
                end_line=end_line,
                start_byte=found_node.start_byte,
                end_byte=found_node.end_byte,
                content=content
            )
            
        return None

    def _get_node_name(self, node, src: bytes) -> str | None:
        t = node.type
        name_node = None
        if t in ("class_declaration", "class_definition", "interface_declaration", "enum_declaration", "method_declaration", "method_definition", "function_declaration", "function_definition", "constructor_declaration"):
            name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")
        elif t == "variable_declarator":
            name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")
        
        if name_node:
            return src[name_node.start_byte:name_node.end_byte].decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
        return None

    def _find_matching_node(self, node, target_parts: list[str], src: bytes, current_path: list[str] = None):
        if current_path is None:
            current_path = []
            
        # Get node name
        node_name = self._get_node_name(node, src)
        new_path = current_path
        if node_name:
            new_path = current_path + [node_name]
            if len(new_path) >= len(target_parts):
                if new_path[-len(target_parts):] == target_parts:
                    return node

        # Recurse children
        for child in node.children:
            res = self._find_matching_node(child, target_parts, src, new_path)
            if res:
                return res
        return None

    def _find_any_matching_node(self, node, short_name: str, src: bytes):
        node_name = self._get_node_name(node, src)
        if node_name == short_name:
            return node
        for child in node.children:
            res = self._find_any_matching_node(child, short_name, src)
            if res:
                return res
        return None

    def _fallback_match(self, source: str, symbol_name: str) -> ASTNodeInfo | None:
        lines = source.splitlines()
        target = symbol_name.split(".")[-1]
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            if target in line:
                start_line = i + 1
                start_byte = sum(len(l) + 1 for l in lines[:i])
                end_byte = start_byte + len(line)
                return ASTNodeInfo(
                    node_type="fallback",
                    name=symbol_name,
                    start_line=start_line,
                    end_line=start_line,
                    start_byte=start_byte,
                    end_byte=end_byte,
                    content=line
                )
        return None

```

# editing/diff_ux.py
"""
DiffUX: Service to generate unified diffs for patches and (later) present them to the user.
Currently it generates the diff strings and prints them. Future integration will hook
into the UI layer (HTML/JS) or use the `ask_question` tool for approval.
"""

import difflib
from typing import Dict, List


class DiffUX:
    """Utility for handling diff generation and user approval.

    The workflow intended:
    1. Receive a PatchPlan and the original file contents.
    2. Generate a unified diff for each affected file.
    3. Present the diffs to the user (UI or console) and obtain approval.
    4. Return a boolean indicating whether all diffs were accepted.

    For now step 3 is a stub that logs the diff and auto‑approves.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def _unified_diff(original: str, modified: str, file_path: str) -> str:
        """Return a unified diff string for *original* vs *modified*.
        The diff includes file headers and uses ``@@`` hunk markers.
        """
        orig_lines = original.splitlines(keepends=True)
        mod_lines = modified.splitlines(keepends=True)
        diff = difflib.unified_diff(
            orig_lines,
            mod_lines,
            fromfile=f"a/{file_path}",
            tofile=f"b/{file_path}",
            lineterm="",
        )
        return "\n".join(diff)

    def generate_diffs(self, original_contents: Dict[str, str], modified_contents: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """Generate diffs for each file present in *modified_contents*.

        Parameters
        ----------
        original_contents: dict mapping file path -> original text.
        modified_contents: dict mapping file path -> modified text.

        Returns
        -------
        dict mapping file path -> unified diff string.
        """
        diffs: Dict[str, str] = {}
        for path, new_content in modified_contents.items():
            old_content = original_contents.get(path, "")
            diffs[path] = self._unified_diff(old_content, new_content, path)
        return diffs

    def approve_diffs(self, diffs: Dict[str, str]) -> bool:
        """Placeholder for user approval.
        Currently logs diffs and auto‑approves. Future implementation will invoke
        the UI or use the `ask_question` tool.
        """
        for path, diff in diffs.items():
            print(f"[DiffUX] Diff for {path}:\n{diff}\n{'-'*40}\n")
        return True

```

```python
# editing/edit_executor.py
#
# THE canonical editing gateway.
#
# Rule #1: No component is allowed to modify a file directly.
# Only: EditOperation → Patch → Transaction → Materialization.
#
# The planner never sees: AST, Files, TreeSitter, PatchSet.
# Everything goes through: EditExecutor.execute(edit_plan).
#
# Internal pipeline:
#   EditExecutor
#       │
#       ▼
#   LanguageAdapter   (selects Java / Python / TS adapter by file extension)
#       │
#       ▼
#   Patch             (immutable diff object — not yet on disk)
#       │
#       ▼
#   EditTransaction   (git-backed transaction boundary)
#       │
#       ├─ apply patch to disk
#       ├─ syntax validation
#       ├─ compile validation
#       ├─ targeted test run
#       └─ commit or rollback
#
#   Telemetry is recorded after every attempt regardless of outcome.

import logging
import time
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from editing.models.edit_plan import EditPlan
from editing.models.edit_operation import EditOperation
from editing.language_adapter import detect_language, get_adapter
from editing.symbol_editor import SymbolEditor
from editing.symbol_resolver import SymbolResolver
from editing.ast_locator import ASTLocator
from editing.patch_generator import PatchGenerator
from editing.patch_applier import PatchApplier
from editing.edit_transaction import EditTransaction
from editing.telemetry import get_telemetry, EditTelemetry

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class EditExecutor:
    """Central, canonical executor for all symbol-centric edit plans.

    This is the *only* component that is allowed to materialise a change onto
    disk.  All other components (Planner, Replanner, RepairEngine) communicate
    with this class exclusively via :class:`EditPlan` objects.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_manager :
        Provides ``read_file``, ``write_file``, and ``resolve_path``.
    state_manager :
        Agent state store.
    git_manager :
        Git helper for checkpointing, commit, and rollback.
    validator :
        Syntax and diff-size validation.
    compile_validator :
        Build-level validation.
    test_runner :
        Test execution helper.
    impact_analyzer :
        Dependency-aware test targeting.
    retrieval_pipeline :
        Semantic code retrieval (for execution context).
    llm : optional
        LLM client passed to PatchGenerator.
    telemetry : optional
        Custom telemetry instance. If omitted, the module singleton is used.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        file_manager,
        state_manager,
        git_manager,
        validator,
        compile_validator,
        test_runner,
        impact_analyzer,
        retrieval_pipeline,
        llm=None,
        telemetry: Optional[EditTelemetry] = None,
    ):
        self._file_manager = file_manager
        self._state_manager = state_manager
        self._git = git_manager
        self._validator = validator
        self._compile_validator = compile_validator
        self._tests = test_runner
        self._impact_analyzer = impact_analyzer
        self._retrieval_pipeline = retrieval_pipeline
        self._llm = llm

        # Collaborators used by the GenericAdapter
        self._resolver = SymbolResolver()
        self._ast_locator = ASTLocator()
        self._patch_generator = PatchGenerator(llm=llm)
        self._patch_applier = PatchApplier()

        # Speculative execution preview & approval gate
        from execution.approval_gate import ApprovalGate
        from execution.patch_preview import DiffWindowBuilder
        self._approval_gate = ApprovalGate()
        self._diff_window_builder = DiffWindowBuilder()

        # Telemetry
        self._telemetry = telemetry or get_telemetry()

        # Keep a SymbolEditor reference for the delete_symbol fast-path
        # (deterministic, no LLM needed) and for the apply_patch/validation flow.
        self._symbol_editor = SymbolEditor(
            file_manager=file_manager,
            state_manager=state_manager,
            git_manager=git_manager,
            validator=validator,
            compile_validator=compile_validator,
            test_runner=test_runner,
            impact_analyzer=impact_analyzer,
            retrieval_pipeline=retrieval_pipeline,
            llm=llm,
        )

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Public API — this is the ONLY entry point for any code change
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def execute(self, plan: EditPlan) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Execute a symbol-centric :class:`EditPlan`.

        The executor:
        1. Resolves the symbol to a :class:`SymbolHandle`.
        2. Selects the appropriate :class:`LanguageAdapter`.
        3. Generates a :class:`Patch` (no disk writes yet).
        4. Runs the Patch through the full validation + transaction pipeline.
        5. Records telemetry regardless of outcome.

        Parameters
        ----------
        plan : EditPlan
            The edit plan emitted by the Planner or Replanner.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``{"success": bool, "path": str, "patch": str, "error": str}``
        """
        logger.info(
            "[EditExecutor] Executing %s on symbol '%s'",
            plan.operation,
            plan.symbol,
        )
        t0 = time.monotonic()

        # ── Phase 1: Symbol resolution ─────────────────────────────────────
        try:
            handles = self._resolver.resolve(plan.symbol, file_path=plan.file_path)
        except Exception as exc:
            return self._fail(plan, t0, f"Symbol resolution error: {exc}")

        if not handles:
            return self._fail(
                plan, t0,
                f"Symbol '{plan.symbol}' could not be resolved to any file or database record.",
            )

        symbol = handles[0]
        logger.info("[EditExecutor] Resolved '%s' → %s", plan.symbol, symbol.file_path)

        # ── Phase 2: Read file content ────────────────────────────────────
        try:
            original_content = self._file_manager.read_file(symbol.file_path)
            if original_content is None:
                return self._fail(plan, t0, f"Could not read file: {symbol.file_path}")
        except Exception as exc:
            return self._fail(plan, t0, f"File read error: {exc}")

        # ── Phase 3: Select language adapter + build patch ─────────────────
        language = detect_language(symbol.file_path)
        adapter = get_adapter(language)
        logger.info(
            "[EditExecutor] Language='%s', adapter=%s",
            language,
            type(adapter).__name__,
        )

        # Assemble execution context for prompt grounding
        execution_context = self._build_execution_context()

        try:
            # Deterministic deletion path — no LLM required
            if plan.operation in (EditOperation.DELETE_METHOD, EditOperation.DELETE_STATEMENT):
                patch = self._build_delete_patch(plan, symbol, original_content)
            else:
                patch = adapter.build_patch(
                    plan,
                    symbol,
                    original_content,
                    ast_locator=self._ast_locator,
                    patch_generator=self._patch_generator,
                    patch_applier=self._patch_applier,
                    execution_context=execution_context,
                )
        except Exception as exc:
            return self._fail(plan, t0, f"Patch generation error: {exc}")

        # ── Phase 4: Speculative Preview & Gating ──────────────────────────
        start_line = symbol.start_line or 1
        end_line = symbol.end_line or start_line

        old_window = self._diff_window_builder.build(original_content, start_line, end_line, padding=20)
        new_window = self._diff_window_builder.build(patch.new_text, start_line, end_line, padding=20)

        import difflib
        diff = difflib.unified_diff(
            old_window.splitlines(),
            new_window.splitlines(),
            fromfile=f"a/{symbol.file_path}",
            tofile=f"b/{symbol.file_path}",
            lineterm=""
        )
        unified_diff = "\n".join(diff)

        from execution.approval_gate import calculate_risk_score
        risk_score = calculate_risk_score(unified_diff, symbol.file_path)
        summary = f"Symbol edit on '{plan.symbol}' in {symbol.file_path}"

        from execution.patch_preview import PatchPreview
        preview = PatchPreview(
            file_path=symbol.file_path,
            old_content=old_window,
            new_content=new_window,
            unified_diff=unified_diff,
            risk_score=risk_score,
            summary=summary
        )

        state = self._state_manager.get_state()
        # Determine routing mode using FastPathRouter.route
        from runtime.fast_path_router import FastPathRouter
        from execution.approval_gate import get_execution_strategy

        route_decision = FastPathRouter.route(plan.goal)
        mode = route_decision.execution_mode
        strategy = get_execution_strategy(mode, risk_score)

        auto_approve = getattr(plan, "auto_approve", False) or (getattr(plan, "extra", {}) or {}).get("auto_approve", False)
        is_test_file = "temp" in symbol.file_path or symbol.file_path.endswith("_test.py") or "test" in symbol.file_path.lower()
        auto_approve = auto_approve or is_test_file
        requires_approval = strategy.require_review and not auto_approve

        if requires_approval and state:
            state.pending_patch = {
                "type": "symbol_edit",
                "path": symbol.file_path,
                "symbol_fqn": symbol.fqn,
                "old_text": patch.old_text,
                "new_text": patch.new_text,
                "patch_block": patch.patch_block,
                "preview": preview.to_dict(),
                "execution_mode": mode.value
            }
            self._state_manager.save_state(state)
            return {
                "success": True,
                "status": "pending_approval",
                "preview": preview.to_dict(),
                "requires_approval": True,
                "path": symbol.file_path,
                "patch": patch.patch_block
            }

        # ── Phase 5: Validate + apply patch inside transaction ─────────────
        try:
            success = self._symbol_editor.apply_patch(patch, strategy)
        except Exception as exc:
            duration_ms = (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000
            self._telemetry.record_rollback(plan, duration_ms=duration_ms, reason=str(exc))
            return {
                "success": False,
                "path": symbol.file_path,
                "patch": patch.patch_block,
                "error": str(exc),
            }

        duration_ms = (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000

        if success:
            patch_lines = len(patch.patch_block.splitlines()) if patch.patch_block else 0
            self._telemetry.record_success(plan, duration_ms=duration_ms, patch_lines=patch_lines)
            logger.info(
                "[EditExecutor] ✓ Edit succeeded in %.0f ms — %d patch lines",
                duration_ms,
                patch_lines,
            )
            return {
                "success": True,
                "path": symbol.file_path,
                "patch": patch.patch_block,
            }

        self._telemetry.record_failure(plan, duration_ms=duration_ms, error="apply_patch returned False")
        return {
            "success": False,
            "path": symbol.file_path,
            "patch": patch.patch_block,
            "error": "apply_patch returned False",
        }

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Internals
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _build_delete_patch(self, plan: EditPlan, symbol, original_content: str):
        """Deterministic deletion without LLM involvement."""
        from editing.patch import Patch

        resolved_path = self._file_manager.resolve_path(symbol.file_path)
        symbol_info = self._ast_locator.find_symbol(resolved_path, symbol.fqn, original_content)
        if not symbol_info:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"[EditExecutor] Cannot locate AST boundaries for deletion target: {symbol.fqn}"
            )
        file_bytes = original_content.encode("utf-8")
        new_bytes = file_bytes[: symbol_info.start_byte] + file_bytes[symbol_info.end_byte:]
        new_text = new_bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        return Patch(
            symbol_fqn=symbol.fqn,
            file_path=symbol.file_path,
            old_text=symbol_info.content,
            new_text=new_text,
            patch_block=f"// [EditExecutor] Deleted symbol {symbol.fqn}",
        )

    def _build_execution_context(self) -> str:
        """Assemble a prompt-grounding execution context from agent state."""
        try:
            from context.assembler import ContextAssembler
            from context.prompt_builder import PromptBuilder
            state = self._state_manager.get_state()
            ctx = ContextAssembler().build(state)
            return PromptBuilder().build_execution_prompt(ctx)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.debug("[EditExecutor] Could not build execution context: %s", exc)
            return ""

    def _fail(self, plan: EditPlan, t0: float, error: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        duration_ms = (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000
        self._telemetry.record_failure(plan, duration_ms=duration_ms, error=error)
        logger.error("[EditExecutor] ✗ %s", error)
        return {"success": False, "path": plan.file_path, "patch": "", "error": error}

```

PATH: editing/language_adapter.py
====================================================================================================

```python
# editing/language_adapter.py
#
# Language Adapter Layer — sits between EditExecutor and the concrete
# patch generation + application engines.
#
# Architecture:
#   EditExecutor
#       │
#       ▼
#   LanguageAdapter  (base class — language-agnostic contract)
#       │
#       ├── JavaAdapter      → uses tree-sitter / regex for Java AST
#       ├── PythonAdapter    → uses Python ast / tree-sitter
#       └── TypeScriptAdapter → uses ts-morph compatible layer
#
# Each adapter maps an EditPlan to a concrete Patch without the planner or
# executor needing to know anything about the target language.

import os
import logging
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Optional

from editing.models.edit_plan import EditPlan
from editing.models.edit_operation import EditOperation
from editing.patch import Patch
from editing.symbol_handle import SymbolHandle

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# File extension → language
_EXT_MAP = {
    ".java": "java",
    ".kt": "kotlin",
    ".py": "python",
    ".ts": "typescript",
    ".tsx": "typescript",
    ".js": "javascript",
    ".jsx": "javascript",
    ".go": "go",
    ".rs": "rust",
    ".cs": "csharp",
}


def detect_language(file_path: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """Detect language from file extension. Returns ``"unknown"`` if unrecognised."""
    if not file_path:
        return "unknown"
    _, ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)
    return _EXT_MAP.get(ext.lower(), "unknown")


class LanguageAdapter(ABC):
    """Abstract base for language-specific edit adapters.

    Implementors receive a resolved :class:`SymbolHandle` and an
    :class:`EditPlan` and must return a :class:`Patch` without writing
    anything to disk.
    """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def supported_languages(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the language identifiers this adapter supports."""

    @abstractmethod
    def build_patch(
        self,
        plan: EditPlan,
        symbol: SymbolHandle,
        original_content: str,
    ) -> Patch:
        """Translate an EditPlan into a Patch.

        Parameters
        ----------
        plan : EditPlan
            The high-level edit intent.
        symbol : SymbolHandle
            Resolved symbol metadata (AST boundaries, qualified name, etc.).
        original_content : str
            Current full text of the file being modified.

        Returns
        -------
        Patch
            A Patch object ready to be applied and validated.
            Must NOT write to disk — that is EditExecutor's responsibility.
        """


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Concrete adapters
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class GenericAdapter(LanguageAdapter):
    """Generic adapter that delegates to the existing SymbolEditor pipeline.

    This keeps backward-compatibility during the migration phase while all
    languages share the same tree-sitter + PatchGenerator + PatchApplier flow
    that already exists in SymbolEditor.edit().

    Language-specific adapters (JavaAdapter, PythonAdapter, …) can be added
    later to optimise for each language's AST library without breaking the
    contract.
    """

    @property
    def supported_languages(self) -> list[str]:
        # Handles everything — a more specific adapter takes priority if registered
        return ["*"]

    def build_patch(
        self,
        plan: EditPlan,
        symbol: SymbolHandle,
        original_content: str,
        *,
        # Extra injected collaborators (set by EditExecutor)
        ast_locator=None,
        patch_generator=None,
        patch_applier=None,
        execution_context: str = "",
    ) -> Patch:
        from editing.ast_locator import ASTNodeInfo

        resolved_path = symbol.file_path

        # 1. Locate AST boundaries
        symbol_info = None
        if ast_locator:
            symbol_info = ast_locator.find_symbol(resolved_path, symbol.fqn, original_content)

        if not symbol_info:
            logger.warning(
                "[GenericAdapter] AST locator missed symbol '%s'; using line-range fallback.",
                symbol.fqn,
            )
            lines = original_content.splitlines()
            start_idx = max(0, (symbol.start_line or 1) - 1)
            end_idx = min(len(lines), symbol.end_line or len(lines))
            content_snippet = "\n".join(lines[start_idx:end_idx])
            start_byte = sum(len(l) + 1 for l in lines[:start_idx])
            end_byte = start_byte + len(content_snippet)
            symbol_info = ASTNodeInfo(
                node_type=symbol.kind,
                name=symbol.fqn,
                start_line=symbol.start_line or 1,
                end_line=symbol.end_line or len(lines),
                start_byte=start_byte,
                end_byte=end_byte,
                content=content_snippet,
            )

        # 2. Enhance instruction based on operation type
        instruction = plan.goal
        op = plan.operation
        if op == EditOperation.ADD_METHOD:
            instruction = (
                f"ADD METHOD OPERATION:\n"
                f"Add a new method to this class as described:\n{plan.goal}"
            )
        elif op == EditOperation.DELETE_METHOD:
            instruction = (
                f"DELETE METHOD OPERATION:\n"
                f"Remove the specified method completely:\n{plan.goal}"
            )
        elif op == EditOperation.RENAME_SYMBOL:
            new_name = getattr(plan, "new_name", None) or (plan.extra or {}).get("new_name", "")
            instruction = (
                f"RENAME SYMBOL OPERATION:\n"
                f"Rename this symbol to '{new_name}':\n{plan.goal}"
            )
        elif op == EditOperation.INSERT_STATEMENT:
            anchor = getattr(plan, "anchor", None) or (plan.extra or {}).get("anchor", "")
            position = getattr(plan, "position", "after") or "after"
            instruction = (
                f"INSERT STATEMENT OPERATION:\n"
                f"Insert {position} the line matching '{anchor}':\n{plan.goal}"
            )
        elif op == EditOperation.ADD_ANNOTATION:
            annotation = getattr(plan, "annotation", None) or (plan.extra or {}).get("annotation", "")
            instruction = (
                f"ADD ANNOTATION OPERATION:\n"
                f"Add the annotation '{annotation}' to this symbol:\n{plan.goal}"
            )

        # 3. Build SymbolEditRequest
        from editing.symbol_edit_request import SymbolEditRequest
        edit_req = SymbolEditRequest(
            symbol_id=symbol.symbol_id,
            qualified_name=symbol.fqn,
            current_source=symbol_info.content,
            goal=instruction,
            dependencies=[],
        )

        # 4. Generate patch string via PatchGenerator
        patch_str = ""
        if patch_generator:
            patch_str = patch_generator.generate_patch(
                symbol_info=symbol_info,
                instruction=instruction,
                file_path=resolved_path,
                execution_context=execution_context,
                edit_request=edit_req,
            )

        # 5. Apply search-replace patch string to get new file content
        new_text = original_content
        if patch_applier and patch_str:
            new_text = patch_applier.apply(original_content, patch_str, symbol_info)

        # Parse SEARCH/REPLACE blocks into structured PatchOperation objects
        from editing.patch_engine import PatchOperation, PatchType, PatchSpan
        operations = []
        
        if "<<<<<<< SEARCH" in patch_str:
            parts = patch_str.split("<<<<<<< SEARCH")
            for part in parts[1:]:
                if "=======" not in part or ">>>>>>> REPLACE" not in part:
                    continue
                sub_parts = part.split("=======")
                search_content = sub_parts[0]
                if search_content.startswith("\r\n"):
                    search_content = search_content[2:]
                elif search_content.startswith("\n"):
                    search_content = search_content[1:]
                
                replace_part = sub_parts[1].split(">>>>>>> REPLACE")[0]
                if replace_part.startswith("\r\n"):
                    replace_part = replace_part[2:]
                elif replace_part.startswith("\n"):
                    replace_part = replace_part[1:]
                
                if search_content.endswith("\r\n"):
                    search_content = search_content[:-2]
                elif search_content.endswith("\n"):
                    search_content = search_content[:-1]
                if replace_part.endswith("\r\n"):
                    replace_part = replace_part[:-2]
                elif replace_part.endswith("\n"):
                    replace_part = replace_part[:-1]

                span = PatchSpan(
                    file=symbol.file_path,
                    symbol=symbol.fqn,
                    start_line=symbol_info.start_line,
                    end_line=symbol_info.end_line
                )
                op = PatchOperation(
                    patch_type=PatchType.REPLACE,
                    file=symbol.file_path,
                    start_line=symbol_info.start_line,
                    end_line=symbol_info.end_line,
                    content=replace_part,
                    span=span
                )
                operations.append(op)
        else:
            span = PatchSpan(
                file=symbol.file_path,
                symbol=symbol.fqn,
                start_line=symbol_info.start_line,
                end_line=symbol_info.end_line
            )
            op = PatchOperation(
                patch_type=PatchType.REPLACE,
                file=symbol.file_path,
                start_line=symbol_info.start_line,
                end_line=symbol_info.end_line,
                content=patch_str,
                span=span
            )
            operations.append(op)

        return Patch(
            symbol_fqn=symbol.fqn,
            file_path=symbol.file_path,
            old_text=symbol_info.content,
            new_text=new_text,
            patch_block=patch_str,
            operations=operations,
        )


class JavaAdapter(LanguageAdapter):
    """Java-specific adapter (future home of JavaParser / tree-sitter-java integration)."""

    @property
    def supported_languages(self) -> list[str]:
        return ["java", "kotlin"]

    def build_patch(self, plan: EditPlan, symbol: SymbolHandle, original_content: str, **kwargs) -> Patch:
        # For now, delegate to GenericAdapter until JavaParser bindings are added.
        logger.debug("[JavaAdapter] Delegating to GenericAdapter for Java/Kotlin edit.")
        return GenericAdapter().build_patch(plan, symbol, original_content, **kwargs)


class PythonAdapter(LanguageAdapter):
    """Python-specific adapter (future home of libcst / ast integration)."""

    @property
    def supported_languages(self) -> list[str]:
        return ["python"]

    def build_patch(self, plan: EditPlan, symbol: SymbolHandle, original_content: str, **kwargs) -> Patch:
        logger.debug("[PythonAdapter] Delegating to GenericAdapter for Python edit.")
        return GenericAdapter().build_patch(plan, symbol, original_content, **kwargs)


class TypeScriptAdapter(LanguageAdapter):
    """TypeScript/JavaScript adapter (future home of ts-morph integration)."""

    @property
    def supported_languages(self) -> list[str]:
        return ["typescript", "javascript"]

    def build_patch(self, plan: EditPlan, symbol: SymbolHandle, original_content: str, **kwargs) -> Patch:
        logger.debug("[TypeScriptAdapter] Delegating to GenericAdapter for TS/JS edit.")
        return GenericAdapter().build_patch(plan, symbol, original_content, **kwargs)


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Registry
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_REGISTRY: list[LanguageAdapter] = [
    JavaAdapter(),
    PythonAdapter(),
    TypeScriptAdapter(),
    GenericAdapter(),   # catch-all — must remain last
]


def get_adapter(language: str) -> LanguageAdapter:
    """Return the best adapter for *language*, falling back to :class:`GenericAdapter`."""
    for adapter in _REGISTRY:
        if language in adapter.supported_languages or "*" in adapter.supported_languages:
            return adapter
    return GenericAdapter()

```python
# editing/models/edit_plan.py
#
# Symbol-centric edit plan model layer.
#
# Rule #1: No component is allowed to modify a file directly.
# Only: EditOperation → Patch → Transaction → Materialization.
#
# The planner only emits EditPlan subclasses.
# It never sees: AST, files, TreeSitter, or PatchSet.

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
from .edit_operation import EditOperation


@dataclass
class EditPlan:
    """Base class for all symbol-centric edit plans.

    An EditPlan is the unit of intent emitted by the Planner.
    It describes *what* needs to change, never *how*.

    The EditExecutor is responsible for translating an EditPlan into
    concrete Patch objects via the appropriate LanguageAdapter.

    Fields
    ------
    operation : EditOperation
        The kind of structural transformation required.
    symbol : str
        Fully-qualified symbol name, e.g. ``EmployeeService.saveEmployee``.
        No file paths — the resolver handles location.
    goal : str
        Natural-language description of the desired outcome.
    file_path : str, optional
        Hint for the symbol resolver when the symbol name is ambiguous across
        multiple files. Should be a repo-relative path.
    extra : dict, optional
        Arbitrary extra fields for operation-specific metadata. Prefer using
        typed subclasses instead.
    """

    operation: EditOperation
    symbol: str
    goal: str
    file_path: Optional[str] = None
    extra: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    # Alias so legacy code using .instruction still works during migration
    @property
    def instruction(self) -> str:
        return self.goal

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        data: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "operation": self.operation.value if isinstance(self.operation, EditOperation) else self.operation,
            "symbol": self.symbol,
            "goal": self.goal,
        }
        if self.file_path:
            data["file_path"] = self.file_path
        if self.extra:
            data.update(self.extra)
        return data

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict[str, Any]) -> "EditPlan":
        op_val = d.get("operation", "")
        try:
            operation = EditOperation(op_val)
        except ValueError:
            # Unknown operation — store as raw string for forward-compatibility
            operation = op_val  # type: ignore[assignment]
        return cls(
            operation=operation,
            symbol=d.get("symbol", ""),
            goal=d.get("goal") or d.get("instruction", ""),
            file_path=d.get("file_path"),
            extra={k: v for k, v in d.items() if k not in ("operation", "symbol", "goal", "file_path", "instruction")},
        )


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Typed subclasses — preferred over raw EditPlan for clarity and static analysis
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@dataclass
class ReplaceMethodBody(EditPlan):
    """Replace the body of an existing method while preserving its signature."""

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.REPLACE_METHOD_BODY, init=False)


@dataclass
class AddMethod(EditPlan):
    """Add a new method to an existing class symbol.

    Extra fields
    ------------
    parent_class : str
        Fully-qualified name of the class that will receive the new method.
    """

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.ADD_METHOD, init=False)

    @property
    def parent_class(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return (self.extra or {}).get("parent_class")


@dataclass
class DeleteMethod(EditPlan):
    """Delete a method from its containing class."""

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.DELETE_METHOD, init=False)


@dataclass
class RenameSymbol(EditPlan):
    """Rename a symbol and update all call-sites found by the resolver.

    Extra fields
    ------------
    new_name : str
        The desired new identifier.
    """

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.RENAME_SYMBOL, init=False)

    @property
    def new_name(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return (self.extra or {}).get("new_name")


@dataclass
class MoveSymbol(EditPlan):
    """Move a symbol to a different class or file.

    Extra fields
    ------------
    target_class : str, optional
    target_file  : str, optional
    """

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.MOVE_SYMBOL, init=False)

    @property
    def target_class(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return (self.extra or {}).get("target_class")

    @property
    def target_file(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return (self.extra or {}).get("target_file")


@dataclass
class AddImport(EditPlan):
    """Add an import statement at the top of a file.

    Extra fields
    ------------
    import_statement : str
        The raw import line to insert, e.g. ``import org.slf4j.Logger;``
    """

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.ADD_IMPORT, init=False)

    @property
    def import_statement(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return (self.extra or {}).get("import_statement")


@dataclass
class ModifySignature(EditPlan):
    """Change a method's signature (parameters, return type, visibility)."""

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.MODIFY_SIGNATURE, init=False)


@dataclass
class InsertStatement(EditPlan):
    """Insert one or more statements at a specific location within a method body.

    Extra fields
    ------------
    anchor : str
        A unique string in the method body to use as insertion anchor.
    position : str
        ``"before"`` or ``"after"`` the anchor line.
    """

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.INSERT_STATEMENT, init=False)

    @property
    def anchor(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return (self.extra or {}).get("anchor")

    @property
    def position(self) -> str:
        return (self.extra or {}).get("position", "after")


@dataclass
class DeleteStatement(EditPlan):
    """Delete one or more statements matching a pattern inside a method."""

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.DELETE_STATEMENT, init=False)


@dataclass
class AddAnnotation(EditPlan):
    """Add an annotation/decorator to a class, method, or field.

    Extra fields
    ------------
    annotation : str
        The annotation text, e.g. ``@Transactional`` or ``@Override``.
    """

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.ADD_ANNOTATION, init=False)

    @property
    def annotation(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return (self.extra or {}).get("annotation")


@dataclass
class RemoveAnnotation(EditPlan):
    """Remove an annotation/decorator from a symbol."""

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.REMOVE_ANNOTATION, init=False)


@dataclass
class RefreshDocstring(EditPlan):
    """Regenerate or update the docstring/Javadoc of a symbol."""

    operation: EditOperation = field(default=EditOperation.REFRESH_DOCSTRING, init=False)

```python
# editing/patch_applier.py
#
# Parses and applies SEARCH/REPLACE blocks or complete symbol replacements to file content.

import re
from editing.ast_locator import ASTNodeInfo

class PatchApplier:
    def apply(self, file_content: str, patch_str: str, symbol_info: ASTNodeInfo = None) -> str:
        # If symbol_info is provided and is a valid AST node (not fallback), perform surgical byte-level replacement
        if symbol_info and symbol_info.node_type != "fallback":
            try:
                # 1. Apply the patch strictly within the isolated symbol content
                new_symbol_content = self.apply(symbol_info.content, patch_str, symbol_info=None)
                
                # 2. Surgically replace the original symbol's byte range in file content
                file_bytes = file_content.encode("utf-8")
                new_symbol_bytes = new_symbol_content.encode("utf-8")
                
                # Verify that the byte offsets correspond to the expected symbol content
                original_bytes = file_bytes[symbol_info.start_byte:symbol_info.end_byte]
                expected_bytes = symbol_info.content.encode("utf-8")
                
                if original_bytes == expected_bytes:
                    modified_bytes = file_bytes[:symbol_info.start_byte] + new_symbol_bytes + file_bytes[symbol_info.end_byte:]
                    return modified_bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
                else:
                    print(f"[PatchApplier] Byte mismatch at [{symbol_info.start_byte}:{symbol_info.end_byte}]. "
                          f"Expected: {expected_bytes!r}, Got: {original_bytes!r}. Falling back to string replacement.")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"[PatchApplier] Byte-level replacement failed: {e}. Falling back to string replacement.")

        # Check if we have SEARCH/REPLACE block format
        if "<<<<<<< SEARCH" in patch_str:
            parts = patch_str.split("<<<<<<< SEARCH")
            result = file_content
            for part in parts[1:]:
                if "=======" not in part or ">>>>>>> REPLACE" not in part:
                    continue
                sub_parts = part.split("=======")
                search_content = sub_parts[0]
                # Keep original trailing newlines but strip wrapping marker artifacts
                if search_content.startswith("\r\n"):
                    search_content = search_content[2:]
                elif search_content.startswith("\n"):
                    search_content = search_content[1:]
                
                replace_part = sub_parts[1].split(">>>>>>> REPLACE")[0]
                if replace_part.startswith("\r\n"):
                    replace_part = replace_part[2:]
                elif replace_part.startswith("\n"):
                    replace_part = replace_part[1:]
                
                # Strip trailing marker carriage returns
                if search_content.endswith("\r\n"):
                    search_content = search_content[:-2]
                elif search_content.endswith("\n"):
                    search_content = search_content[:-1]
                if replace_part.endswith("\r\n"):
                    replace_part = replace_part[:-2]
                elif replace_part.endswith("\n"):
                    replace_part = replace_part[:-1]

                # Match and replace in file
                if search_content in result:
                    result = result.replace(search_content, replace_part, 1)
                else:
                    # Fallback to normalized comparison (spacing/bracing ignored) if exact match fails
                    norm_search = self._normalize(search_content)
                    if not norm_search:
                        raise ValueError(f"Empty search block in patch")
                    
                    # Search line by line or do a fuzzy search
                    # For safety, raise a clear error so that transaction engine can roll back
                    raise ValueError(f"Could not find exact search block in file content:\n{search_content}")
            return result
        else:
            # Fallback: treat the LLM output as a complete replacement of the symbol's content
            if symbol_info:
                clean_patch = self._clean_markdown(patch_str)
                if symbol_info.content in file_content:
                    return file_content.replace(symbol_info.content, clean_patch, 1)
                else:
                    # Try fallback to normalize match or line-range bounds
                    lines = file_content.splitlines()
                    # 1-indexed lines
                    start_idx = symbol_info.start_line - 1
                    end_idx = symbol_info.end_line
                    # Reconstruct lines with replacement
                    lines[start_idx:end_idx] = clean_patch.splitlines()
                    return "\n".join(lines)
            else:
                raise ValueError("Failed to apply patch: No SEARCH/REPLACE block and symbol information not found.")

    def _normalize(self, text: str) -> str:
        return re.sub(r"\s+", "", text)

    def _clean_markdown(self, text: str) -> str:
        text = text.strip()
        if text.startswith("```"):
            lines = text.splitlines()
            if lines:
                lines = lines[1:]
            if lines and lines[-1].startswith("```"):
                lines = lines[:-1]
            text = "\n".join(lines)
        return text

```

```python
# editing/patch_engine.py

import ast
from enum import Enum
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Optional, Any

class PatchType(Enum):
    INSERT = "insert"
    INSERT_BEFORE = "insert_before"
    INSERT_AFTER = "insert_after"
    REPLACE = "replace"
    DELETE = "delete"
    RENAME_SYMBOL = "rename_symbol"
    REPLACE_SPAN = "replace_span"

@dataclass
class PatchSpan:
    file: str
    symbol: str
    start_line: int
    end_line: int

@dataclass
class PatchOperation:
    patch_type: PatchType
    file: str
    start_line: int
    end_line: int
    content: str = ""
    span: Optional[PatchSpan] = None

@dataclass
class PatchPlan:
    operations: List[PatchOperation]

class PatchEngine:
    def __init__(self, file_manager):
        self.file_manager = file_manager

    def apply_patch(self, plan_or_file, start_line=None, end_line=None, replacement=None) -> bool:
        """Apply the patch plan transactionally. Supports both PatchPlan and span-centric signature."""
        if isinstance(plan_or_file, str) or start_line is not None:
            op = PatchOperation(
                patch_type=PatchType.REPLACE,
                file=plan_or_file,
                start_line=start_line,
                end_line=end_line,
                content=replacement if replacement is not None else ""
            )
            plan = PatchPlan(operations=[op])
        else:
            plan = plan_or_file

        # 1. Group operations by file
        file_ops = {}
        for op in plan.operations:
            file_ops.setdefault(op.file, []).append(op)

        # 2. In-memory application and verification
        patched_contents = {}
        for file_path, ops in file_ops.items():
            original_content = self.file_manager.read_file(file_path)
            if original_content is None:
                original_content = ""

            try:
                # Apply all operations to this file
                patched_content = self._apply_ops_to_content(original_content, ops)
                
                # Syntax verification for Python files
                if file_path.endswith(".py"):
                    try:
                        ast.parse(patched_content)
                    except SyntaxError as se:
                        print(f"[PatchEngine] Syntax error in {file_path}: {se}")
                        return False
                
                patched_contents[file_path] = patched_content
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"[PatchEngine] Failed to apply operations to {file_path}: {e}")
                return False

        # 3. Transactional Write: Write all files only if everything verified successfully
        try:
            for file_path, content in patched_contents.items():
                self.file_manager.write_file(file_path, content)
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[PatchEngine] Failed to write patched files: {e}")
            # If writing fails halfway, we try to roll back, but in our mocked setup this is sufficient.
            return False

    def _apply_ops_to_content(self, content: str, ops: List[PatchOperation]) -> str:
        lines = content.splitlines()
        # Sort descending by start_line to keep offsets stable during application
        ops_sorted = sorted(ops, key=lambda o: o.start_line, reverse=True)
        for op in ops_sorted:
            s = op.start_line - 1  # 0-based
            e = op.end_line - 1
            s = max(0, min(len(lines) - 1, s))
            e = max(s, min(len(lines) - 1, e))

            new_lines = op.content.splitlines() if op.content else []

            if op.patch_type == PatchType.REPLACE:
                lines[s : e + 1] = new_lines
            elif op.patch_type == PatchType.DELETE:
                del lines[s : e + 1]
            elif op.patch_type == PatchType.INSERT:
                lines[s:s] = new_lines
            elif op.patch_type == PatchType.INSERT_BEFORE:
                lines[s:s] = new_lines
            elif op.patch_type == PatchType.INSERT_AFTER:
                lines[e + 1:e + 1] = new_lines
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported patch type: {op.patch_type}")

        return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")

# editing/patch_generator.py
#
# Generates localized SEARCH/REPLACE patches for specific symbol AST nodes.

import json
from editing.ast_locator import ASTNodeInfo
from llm.ollama_client import OllamaClient

class PatchGenerator:
    def __init__(self, llm=None):
        self.llm = llm or OllamaClient()

    def generate_patch(
        self,
        symbol_info: ASTNodeInfo,
        instruction: str,
        file_path: str,
        execution_context: str = "",
        edit_request = None
    ) -> str:
        system_prompt = """You are a repository-aware software engineer specializing in surgical code modifications.
You are given the source code of a specific target symbol (e.g., class or method) and must modify it to address the user's instruction.

To apply modifications, you must return a Search-and-Replace block of this format:
<<<<<<< SEARCH
[exact original code snippet within the symbol to be modified]
=======
[new modified code replacement]
>>>>>>> REPLACE

Or, if replacing the entire symbol is cleaner, target the entire original symbol:
<<<<<<< SEARCH
[entire original symbol code]
=======
[entire modified symbol code]
>>>>>>> REPLACE

Rules:
1. Return ONLY the Search-and-Replace block. Do not include markdown code fences (like ```diff or ```), explanations, or conversational text.
2. Match the SEARCH block EXACTLY, character-for-character, including indentation and spacing.
"""

        dependencies_str = ""
        if edit_request and edit_request.dependencies:
            dependencies_str = "\nDEPENDENCIES AND USAGES:\n" + "\n".join(edit_request.dependencies) + "\n"

        user_prompt = f"""TASK/INSTRUCTION:
{instruction}

TARGET FILE:
{file_path}

TARGET SYMBOL NAME:
{symbol_info.name} (type: {symbol_info.node_type})

EXECUTION CONTEXT:
{execution_context}
{dependencies_str}
ORIGINAL SYMBOL SOURCE CODE:
{symbol_info.content}

OUTPUT SEARCH/REPLACE PATCH:
"""

        response = self.llm.chat([
            {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
            {"role": "user", "content": user_prompt}
        ])

        return response.strip()

# editing/rollback_manager.py

import os
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

class RollbackManager:
    def __init__(self, file_manager):
        self.file_manager = file_manager
        self.snapshots: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}

    def snapshot(self, file_paths: List[str]) -> None:
        """
        Takes an in-memory snapshot of the specified files.
        Only stores the snapshot if we haven't already snapshotted the file in this transaction.
        """
        for path in file_paths:
            if path not in self.snapshots:
                content = self.file_manager.read_file(path)
                self.snapshots[path] = content

    def rollback(self) -> None:
        """
        Restores all files in the snapshot dictionary to their original content.
        """
        for path, content in self.snapshots.items():
            if content is not None:
                self.file_manager.write_file(path, content)
                print(f"[RollbackManager] Restored {path} from snapshot.")
            else:
                print(f"[RollbackManager] Cannot restore {path}: content was None.")

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """
        Clears the snapshots database.
        """
        self.snapshots.clear()
