            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

      "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

      "chunk_index": 0,
      "total_chunks": 1,
      "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "chunk_index": 0,

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "chunk_index": 0,

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",
