            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

      "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

      "chunk_index": 0,
      "total_chunks": 1,
      "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

            "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

            "code": "# ADR 0001: Tech stack\n\n- Status: Accepted\n- Date: 2026-05-05\n- Decider: project owner\n\n## Context\n\nWe are building an internal HRMS / Resource Management / Billing Analytics\nplatform with sensitive HR and finance data, role-based access for 7 roles,\naudit requirements, dashboards, and integrations (Slack, S3). The system must\nbe secure, structured, auditable, and easy to extend over a multi-year horizon.\n\n## Decision\n\n| Concern              | Choice                                                              |\n|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Language (backend)   | Java 21 (LTS)                                                        |\n| Framework            | Spring Boot **4.0.6** (released 2026-04-23)                          |\n| Build                | Maven                                                                |\n| Persistence          | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate                                          |\n| Migrations           | Flyway, forward-only                                                 |\n| API style            | Spring MVC `@RestController` (synchronous, blocking)                 |\n| Auth                 | Spring Security as OAuth2 Resource Server, JWT from Keycloak 26      |\n| Validation           | Bean Validation (Jakarta)                                            |\n| API docs             | springdoc-openapi → `/v3/api-docs`, `/swagger-ui`                    |\n| Mapping              | MapStruct                                                            |\n| Boilerplate          | Lombok                                                               |\n| Database             | PostgreSQL 18 (uses native `uuidv7()`)                               |\n| Cache                | Redis 7                                                              |\n| Object storage       | MinIO local, S3 prod, behind one `StorageService` interface          |\n| Background jobs      | Spring `@Scheduled` (no Kafka/Quartz/Rabbit for MVP)                 |\n| Frontend             | React 19 + TypeScript + Vite                                         |\n| Frontend styling     | Tailwind + shadcn/ui                                                 |\n| Frontend data        | TanStack Query (server) + React Hook Form + Zod (forms)              |\n| Charts               | Recharts                                                             |\n| Frontend types       | `openapi-typescript` (types only, no full client codegen)            |\n| Local platform       | Docker Compose (postgres, keycloak, minio, redis)                    |\n\n## Rationale\n\n- Spring Boot is the boring/correct choice for an enterprise CRUD-heavy app\n  with rich auth, scheduling, validation, and JPA needs.\n- PostgreSQL beats MySQL here: better JSON, partial indexes, partitioning,\n  built-in `uuidv7()`, mature analytics patterns, ergonomic for finance data.\n- Keycloak removes a category of bugs we should never write ourselves\n  (login flows, password reset, MFA, token refresh, role admin UI).\n- MapStruct compile-time mapping avoids reflection cost and produces\n  debuggable code, unlike runtime mappers.\n- Lightweight `openapi-typescript` keeps the FE↔BE contract honest without\n  generating an entire SDK that fights TanStack Query idioms.\n- MinIO + S3 with a single `StorageService` means dev parity and zero\n  rewrites when we move to AWS later.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- We commit to Java 21+ and PG 18+. Older infra is unsupported.\n- `pom.xml` pins Spring Boot 4.0.6; bumps require an ADR addendum.\n- Keycloak realm is reproduced from a committed JSON export; UI changes that\n  aren't ported back to JSON are considered rebellion and will be lost on\n  next reset.\n- We will not introduce a second chart, mapping, or HTTP-client library\n  without an ADR.",

      "code": "class RepoContext:\n\n    IMPORTANT_FILES = [\n        \"pom.xml\",\n        \"package.json\",\n        \"README.md\"\n    ]\n\n    IGNORE_DIRS = {\n        \"node_modules\",\n        \".git\",\n        \"__pycache__\",\n        \".venv\",\n        \"venv\",\n        \"dist\",\n        \"build\"\n    }\n\n    IGNORE_EXTENSIONS = {\n        \".png\",\n        \".jpg\",\n        \".jpeg\",\n        \".gif\",\n        \".exe\",\n        \".lock\"\n    }\n\n    def __init__(self, root=\".\"):\n\n        self.root = Path(root)\n\n    def summarize(self, files):\n\n        important = []\n\n        for file in files:\n\n            # Ignore unwanted folders\n            if any(ignore in file for ignore in self.IGNORE_DIRS):\n                continue\n\n            # Ignore unwanted file types\n            if any(file.endswith(ext) for ext in self.IGNORE_EXTENSIONS):\n                continue\n\n            important.append(file)\n\n        important.sort()\n\n        return \"\\n\".join(important[:200])\n\n    def build_summary(self):\n\n        summary = []\n\n        for file in self.IMPORTANT_FILES:\n\n            path = self.root / file\n\n            if path.exists():\n\n                content = path.read_text(\n                    encoding=\"utf-8\",\n                    errors=\"ignore\"\n                )\n\n                summary.append(\n                    f\"\\nFILE: {file}\\n\"\n                )\n\n                summary.append(\n                    content[:3000]\n                )\n\n        return \"\\n\".join(summary)",

      "code": "    def build_summary(self):\n\n        summary = []\n\n        for file in self.IMPORTANT_FILES:\n\n            path = self.root / file\n\n            if path.exists():\n\n                content = path.read_text(\n                    encoding=\"utf-8\",\n                    errors=\"ignore\"\n                )\n\n                summary.append(\n                    f\"\\nFILE: {file}\\n\"\n                )\n\n                summary.append(\n                    content[:3000]\n                )\n\n        return \"\\n\".join(summary)",

      "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

      "parent": null,
      "docstring": "Converts a list of TestFailure dicts (from failure_parser.py) into\nan ordered list of REPAIR Actions with concrete file targets.\n\nUsage in executor dispatch:\n    result = self.tests.run_backend_tests()\n    failures = result.get(\"failures\", [])\n    if failures:\n        actions = self.failure_engine.build_repair_actions(failures, state)\n        state_manager.push_executions(actions)",
      "imports": [
        "typing",
        "planning.action_schema",
        "planning.action_types",
        "os"
      ],
      "chunk_index": 0,
      "total_chunks": 2,
      "code": "class FailureAnalysisEngine:\n    \"\"\"\n    Converts a list of TestFailure dicts (from failure_parser.py) into\n    an ordered list of REPAIR Actions with concrete file targets.\n\n    Usage in executor dispatch:\n        result = self.tests.run_backend_tests()\n        failures = result.get(\"failures\", [])\n        if failures:\n            actions = self.failure_engine.build_repair_actions(failures, state)\n            state_manager.push_executions(actions)\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # =========================================================\n    # MAIN\n    # =========================================================\n\n    def build_repair_actions(\n        self,\n        failures: List[Dict[str, Any]],\n        state,\n        state_manager=None,\n    ) -> List[Action]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Given a list of structured failure dicts, return REPAIR actions\n        with `targets` metadata populated from `likely_source_files`.\n\n        Also writes `state.test_failure_targets` so repair_from_context\n        and RepairEngine can read them without re-parsing.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        # Collect all unique likely source files across all failures,\n        # preserving the order in which they appear (first failure first).\n        all_targets: List[str] = []\n        seen: set = set()\n\n        for failure in failures:\n            for path in failure.get(\"likely_source_files\", []):\n                if path and path not in seen:\n                    seen.add(path)\n                    all_targets.append(path)\n\n        # Fallback: if no source files resolved, use stack frames as hints\n        if not all_targets:\n            for failure in failures:\n                for frame in failure.get(\"stack_frames\", [])[:3]:\n                    hint = frame.split(\":\")[0]  # \"EmployeeService.java\"\n                    if hint not in seen:\n                        seen.add(hint)\n                        all_targets.append(hint)\n\n        # Write back to state so other components can read without re-parsing\n        if state is not None and hasattr(state, \"test_failure_targets\"):\n            state.test_failure_targets = all_targets[:10]\n        elif state is not None:\n            try:\n                object.__setattr__(state, \"test_failure_targets\", all_targets[:10])\n            except Exception:\n                pass\n\n        actions: List[Action] = []\n\n        if not all_targets:\n            # No specific targets resolved — fall back to retrieval-guided repair\n            error_text = self._summarise_failures(failures)\n            actions.append(Action(\n                action_type=RETRIEVE,\n                title=\"Retrieve failure context\",\n                target=error_text,\n                reasoning=\"No source files resolved from stack trace — search by error text\",\n                priority=1,\n            ))\n            actions.append(Action(\n                action_type=REPAIR,\n                title=\"Repair from retrieved context\",\n                target=\"repair failure\",\n                reasoning=\"Guiding repair from retrieval since source files unresolved\",\n                priority=2,\n                blocking=True,\n                metadata={\"targets\": []},\n            ))\n            return actions\n\n        # Build one REPAIR action per unique target file (up to 5)\n        for idx, target_path in enumerate(all_targets[:5]):\n            # Human-readable failure summary for the relevant failure(s)\n            relevant = [\n                f for f in failures\n                if target_path in f.get(\"likely_source_files\", [])\n            ]\n            description = self._summarise_failures(relevant or failures[:1])\n\n            actions.append(Action(\n                action_type=REPAIR,\n                title=f\"Repair {self._basename(target_path)} — {description[:80]}\",\n                target=target_path,\n                reasoning=(\n                    f\"Stack trace points to {self._basename(target_path)}: \"\n                    f\"{description}\"\n                ),\n                priority=idx + 1,\n                blocking=True,\n                metadata={\n                    \"targets\": [target_path],\n                    \"failure_description\": description,\n                    \"all_failure_targets\": all_targets,\n                },\n            ))\n\n        # Always validate + re-run tests after repairs\n        actions.append(Action(\n            action_type=VALIDATE,\n            title=\"Validate repaired files\",\n            target=\"post-repair validation\",\n            reasoning=\"Ensure repairs are syntactically correct\",\n            priority=len(all_targets[:5]) + 1,\n        ))\n\n        return actions\n",

      "chunk_index": 0,
      "total_chunks": 1,
      "code": "class RepoContext:\n\n    IMPORTANT_FILES = [\n        \"pom.xml\",\n        \"package.json\",\n        \"README.md\"\n    ]\n\n    IGNORE_DIRS = {\n        \"node_modules\",\n        \".git\",\n        \"__pycache__\",\n        \".venv\",\n        \"venv\",\n        \"dist\",\n        \"build\"\n    }\n\n    IGNORE_EXTENSIONS = {\n        \".png\",\n        \".jpg\",\n        \".jpeg\",\n        \".gif\",\n        \".exe\",\n        \".lock\"\n    }\n\n    def __init__(self, root=\".\"):\n\n        self.root = Path(root)\n\n    def summarize(self, files):\n\n        important = []\n\n        for file in files:\n\n            # Ignore unwanted folders\n            if any(ignore in file for ignore in self.IGNORE_DIRS):\n                continue\n\n            # Ignore unwanted file types\n            if any(file.endswith(ext) for ext in self.IGNORE_EXTENSIONS):\n                continue\n\n            important.append(file)\n\n        important.sort()\n\n        return \"\\n\".join(important[:200])\n\n    def build_summary(self):\n\n        summary = []\n\n        for file in self.IMPORTANT_FILES:\n\n            path = self.root / file\n\n            if path.exists():\n\n                content = path.read_text(\n                    encoding=\"utf-8\",\n                    errors=\"ignore\"\n                )\n\n                summary.append(\n                    f\"\\nFILE: {file}\\n\"\n                )\n\n                summary.append(\n                    content[:3000]\n                )\n\n        return \"\\n\".join(summary)",

      "code": "    def _summarise_failures(self, failures: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Short human-readable summary of failures for action titles.\"\"\"\n        parts = []\n        for f in failures[:3]:\n            error_type = f.get(\"error_type\", \"\")\n            message = f.get(\"message\", \"\")\n            if error_type and message:\n                parts.append(f\"{error_type}: {message[:60]}\")\n            elif message:\n                parts.append(message[:60])\n        return \"; \".join(parts) if parts else \"test failure\"",

      "docstring": "Converts a list of TestFailure dicts (from failure_parser.py) into\nan ordered list of REPAIR Actions with concrete file targets.\n\nUsage in executor dispatch:\n    result = self.tests.run_backend_tests()\n    failures = result.get(\"failures\", [])\n    if failures:\n        actions = self.failure_engine.build_repair_actions(failures, state)\n        state_manager.push_executions(actions)",
      "imports": [
        "typing",
        "planning.action_schema",
        "planning.action_types",
        "os"
      ],
      "chunk_index": 0,
      "total_chunks": 2,
      "code": "class FailureAnalysisEngine:\n    \"\"\"\n    Converts a list of TestFailure dicts (from failure_parser.py) into\n    an ordered list of REPAIR Actions with concrete file targets.\n\n    Usage in executor dispatch:\n        result = self.tests.run_backend_tests()\n        failures = result.get(\"failures\", [])\n        if failures:\n            actions = self.failure_engine.build_repair_actions(failures, state)\n            state_manager.push_executions(actions)\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # =========================================================\n    # MAIN\n    # =========================================================\n\n    def build_repair_actions(\n        self,\n        failures: List[Dict[str, Any]],\n        state,\n        state_manager=None,\n    ) -> List[Action]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Given a list of structured failure dicts, return REPAIR actions\n        with `targets` metadata populated from `likely_source_files`.\n\n        Also writes `state.test_failure_targets` so repair_from_context\n        and RepairEngine can read them without re-parsing.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        # Collect all unique likely source files across all failures,\n        # preserving the order in which they appear (first failure first).\n        all_targets: List[str] = []\n        seen: set = set()\n\n        for failure in failures:\n            for path in failure.get(\"likely_source_files\", []):\n                if path and path not in seen:\n                    seen.add(path)\n                    all_targets.append(path)\n\n        # Fallback: if no source files resolved, use stack frames as hints\n        if not all_targets:\n            for failure in failures:\n                for frame in failure.get(\"stack_frames\", [])[:3]:\n                    hint = frame.split(\":\")[0]  # \"EmployeeService.java\"\n                    if hint not in seen:\n                        seen.add(hint)\n                        all_targets.append(hint)\n\n        # Write back to state so other components can read without re-parsing\n        if state is not None and hasattr(state, \"test_failure_targets\"):\n            state.test_failure_targets = all_targets[:10]\n        elif state is not None:\n            try:\n                object.__setattr__(state, \"test_failure_targets\", all_targets[:10])\n            except Exception:\n                pass\n\n        actions: List[Action] = []\n\n        if not all_targets:\n            # No specific targets resolved — fall back to retrieval-guided repair\n            error_text = self._summarise_failures(failures)\n            actions.append(Action(\n                action_type=RETRIEVE,\n                title=\"Retrieve failure context\",\n                target=error_text,\n                reasoning=\"No source files resolved from stack trace — search by error text\",\n                priority=1,\n            ))\n            actions.append(Action(\n                action_type=REPAIR,\n                title=\"Repair from retrieved context\",\n                target=\"repair failure\",\n                reasoning=\"Guiding repair from retrieval since source files unresolved\",\n                priority=2,\n                blocking=True,\n                metadata={\"targets\": []},\n            ))\n            return actions\n\n        # Build one REPAIR action per unique target file (up to 5)\n        for idx, target_path in enumerate(all_targets[:5]):\n            # Human-readable failure summary for the relevant failure(s)\n            relevant = [\n                f for f in failures\n                if target_path in f.get(\"likely_source_files\", [])\n            ]\n            description = self._summarise_failures(relevant or failures[:1])\n\n            actions.append(Action(\n                action_type=REPAIR,\n                title=f\"Repair {self._basename(target_path)} — {description[:80]}\",\n                target=target_path,\n                reasoning=(\n                    f\"Stack trace points to {self._basename(target_path)}: \"\n                    f\"{description}\"\n                ),\n                priority=idx + 1,\n                blocking=True,\n                metadata={\n                    \"targets\": [target_path],\n                    \"failure_description\": description,\n                    \"all_failure_targets\": all_targets,\n                },\n            ))\n\n        # Always validate + re-run tests after repairs\n        actions.append(Action(\n            action_type=VALIDATE,\n            title=\"Validate repaired files\",\n            target=\"post-repair validation\",\n            reasoning=\"Ensure repairs are syntactically correct\",\n            priority=len(all_targets[:5]) + 1,\n        ))\n\n        return actions\n",

        "summary": "### Frontend Architecture Overview\n\nThe frontend of the Human Resource Management System (HRMS) is structured around a React application that provides an intuitive interface for users to interact with the system. The application includes several key components and utilities that are essential for its functionality.\n\n#### Components & Configurations\n1. **components.json**\n   - **Role**: This JSON file manages frontend components and configurations.\n   - **Dependencies**:\n     - Tailwind CSS: Integrated for consistent styling across the application.\n     - Lucide Icons: Used to provide a set of icons to enhance UI elements.\n   - **Main Exports**:\n     - Aliases for commonly used directories like `components`, `utils`, `ui`.\n\n2. **Silent Single Sign-On (SSO)**\n   - **silent-check-sso.html**\n     - **Role**: A simple HTML file that facilitates silent SSO by sending the current URL to the parent window using `postMessage`.\n     - **Dependencies**:\n       - Browser APIs for interaction with parent frames.\n     - **Main Exports**: None explicitly exported; performs an action and exits.\n\n### Backend Architecture Overview\n\nThe backend of the HRMS system is built on Java using Spring Boot, providing a robust architecture for handling business logic, security, and data management.\n\n#### Security Management\n1. **CurrentUser.java**\n   - **Role**: Represents the authenticated user in the system.\n   - **Dependencies**:\n     - Spring Security: Utilized for authentication processes.\n   - **Main Exports**:\n     - Methods to check user roles, extract user details, and retrieve the current user instance.\n\n#### Error Handling\n2. **FieldError.java**\n   - **Role**: Represents individual validation errors for fields in API responses.\n   - **Dependencies**: None; self-contained within the same package.\n   - **Main Exports**:\n     - A record with three fields: `field`, `code`, and `message`.\n\n### Additional Scripts\n\n1. **file_discovery.py**\n   - **Role**: A script to discover files within a directory tree while excluding specific directories.\n   - **Dependencies**:\n     - Python's `pathlib` module.\n   - **Main Exports**:\n     - The `discover_files` function.\n\n2. **export_repository_dump.py**\n   - **Role**: Exports the contents of selected folders into a single Markdown file, ignoring certain files and directories.\n   - **Dependencies**:\n     - Python’s `pathlib` for path manipulations.\n   - **Main Exports**:\n     - The repository's contents exported into a Markdown file.\n\n### Integration & Dependencies\n\n- The frontend communicates with the backend through HTTP/HTTPS requests to fetch data, handle user interactions, and manage authentication. This interaction is managed by Spring Security on the backend, ensuring that all requests are authenticated and authorized.\n  \n- The `silent-check-sso.html` script, part of the frontend, facilitates silent SSO by interacting with the parent window via `postMessage`. This allows for a seamless login experience without user intervention.\n\n- The backend scripts (`file_discovery.py`, `export_repository_dump.py`) provide utilities that can be invoked from within the application or as standalone scripts. These scripts help in managing file operations and repository exports, respectively.\n\n### Key Entry Points\n\n- **Frontend Entry Point**: \n  - The main entry point for the frontend React application is typically a file like `index.js` or `main.js`. This file initializes the React app and renders it into the DOM.\n\n- **Backend Entry Point**:\n  - The backend is bootstrapped via a Spring Boot application class, usually annotated with `@SpringBootApplication`.\n\n### Summary\n\nThe frontend of the HRMS system is built on React and provides a user-friendly interface for interacting with various features of the system. It includes components managed by `components.json`, handles SSO silently using `silent-check-sso.html`, and communicates securely with the backend via HTTP/HTTPS requests.\n\nThe backend, written in Java with Spring Boot, manages authentication, authorization, and business logic.
